note: Everything here is provisional. Canon is never minted in a concept register; the implementation audit censuses Plans/UI_Command_Catalog.md and adjudicates exact ids. Longform deliberately reuses the shared-v2 dest grammar for every navigation, so most interactions map onto existing candidate families rather than new ids.

flags.note: One dest-object payload {route, cat?, sub?, managerId?, objectId?, tab?, settingId?, query?, focus?} covers rail links, breadcrumbs, destination rows, manager rows, search selection, recents, and copy-done. No per-destination command ids are needed.
Longform never needed a single hard-coded open-X command; both aliases collapse into cmd.settings.navigate {dest}.
Query text plus limit; results route only by rid/dest. The focus=<rid> route param is the one addition to census (carries the exact landing element through a hash navigation).
sources/preview/apply/rollback map 1:1 onto PM2.copy; apply is a staged op (restore-point, apply, verify) and rollback takes the receipt id.

families_exercised_note: Value mutation always runs through store.setValue (validation, receipts, recents); manager actions always run through def.actions(store).run; nothing dispatches by label or index anywhere in the concept.

new_candidates.note: Selection of a search result must survive a route hop and still land on the exact element (row, object anchor, tab section, action link). Longform encodes the rid in the focus param and re-resolves it after render; the catalog needs one canonical way to say 'navigate and locate'.

Longform's More/Advanced ruled folds are explicit disclosure state, auto-opened by deep links to hidden rows. If other surfaces adopt tiered folds, the open-state mutation should have one id rather than per-concept ad-hoc state.
Close Settings returns to whatever opened Settings (simulated receipt in the concept). Distinct from the Escape ladder, which stops at Home and never exits.
